segments.text: Hey, this is Artronic Electronics! Today: the capacitor, explained simply.
A capacitor is just two metal plates, separated by an insulator. Current can't flow through it… but charges can build up on the plates.
Close the switch: electrons leave one plate and pile up on the other. The capacitor is charging.
It starts fast, then slows down more and more. The voltage follows this curve.
The key number is tau, equal to R times C. After one tau, you reach sixty-three percent. After five tau, it's practically full.
Example: ten kilo-ohms and one hundred microfarads give a tau of one second. Next time: the inductor. Subscribe so you don't miss it!
